title: Context Scheduling & Latency-aware Routing — scratchpad
content:
Quick summary:
- Trying to codify ideas for latency-aware request scheduling across model variants and GPUs. Goal: keep 99th p50 within SLO while lowering cost by opportunistic model-switching + shaping.

Why this matters (notes to self):
- In production we often overprovision for tail latency; customers pay.
- Some requests are latency-sensitive (interactive chat), others are throughput-tolerant (batch reranking).
- If we can classify per-request slack and route accordingly (fast small model / quantized variant / queued batched path) we can save tokens/hours on dedicated pools.

Key ideas & sketches:
1) Per-request slack inference
   - Lightweight estimator on request arrival: tokens remaining distribution + user-specified max_wait (if provided).
   - Feature set: prompt length, user tier, device type (mobile), recent per-user latency tolerance heuristic.
   - Output: slack bucket = {urgent (<50ms), soft (50-200ms), flexible (>200ms)}.

2) Model-switch routing
   - Have policy layers: prefer fast-optimized variant (f32->int8/4bit) for soft/flexible; reserve FP16 or larger for urgent.
   - Safety: quick quality check sample for classes where degradation is risky (e.g., code generation).

3) Opportunistic shaping + preemptible batching
   - If slack > threshold, delay a few ms to coalesce into an existing batch; this reduces per-token GPU overhead.
   - Preemptible background execution for flexible requests (can be paused/resumed) — store KV cache snapshots.

4) Fallback and SLA enforcement
   - Guaranteed path for premium customers: bypass opportunistic shaping.
   - If system under pressure, dynamic escalation: move soft->urgent path if waiting time exceeds predicted deadline.

Related work / inspiration:
- "Latency-aware model switching" (Zhou et al., 2028) — adaptive variant selection using a contextual bandit. Notes: their bandit assumes stable workload; need warm-start heuristics for sudden bursts. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2801.01234)
- SchedLLM repos & internal experiments (my rough impl): github.com/sylvia-khan/sched-explorations — toy env with two variants, sim workload.
- Papers on request shaping and batching in datacenter queues (some older queuing-theory citations I need to re-surf).

Small experiment plan (local sim -> canary -> production):
A) Local sim (2 days)
   - Build synthetic client traces: mix of chat, summarization, embedding requests.
   - Implement simple slack estimator (prompt_len / avg_tok_ms) and three routing policies: always-fast, always-best, slack-policy.
   - Metrics: average cost per request, 50/95/99 latency, quality delta on small eval set (ROUGE/BLEU/semantic sim).

B) Canary on a single Dedicated pool (1 week)
   - Expose policy via feature flag. Route 5% traffic from non-premium customers.
   - Add tracing fields: slack_bucket, chosen_variant, wait_time_before_dispatch, batch_id.

C) Rollout and monitoring (2-4 weeks)
   - Set conservative auto-escalation thresholds. Monitor quality regressions and customer complaints.

Open research questions / unknowns:
- How to quantify quality loss quickly? Need lightweight proxy evaluator that is cheap per request. Possible approach: use distilled critic model (tiny) to score outputs offline and online sample-check ~1% of responses.
- How effective is tiny delay for real coalescing given bursty mobile workloads? We need real traces from web clients.
- KV snapshot cost: memory vs resume latency tradeoffs. Saving per-request KV may be heavy; maybe save only for long-running multi-turn conversations.

Implementation notes / technical debt to track:
- Add metadata hooks to request object for slack and routing decisions (LIN-4821).
- Expose variant cost profile table in Console for SRE/product to tune thresholds.
- Need an eval harness that runs outputs from switched variants vs baseline and computes semantic similarity; tie into Redwood Optimize recommended prompts.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Build local sim harness (priority).
- [ ] Prototype slack estimator code (python) and tiny policy server (go).
- [ ] Add tracing fields to request schema (instrumentation PR).
- [ ] Draft quick internal one-pager for eng + product on tradeoffs and safe defaults.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- "soft" bucket could itself be split by model fragility: e.g., knowledge-grounded responses shouldn't be auto-quantized without context checks.
- Consider per-customer policy overrides at Console level (GTM ask).
- Could combine with cache hints: if prefix found in KV cache, route to fast variant since generation cost is small.

Sample prompts for light evaluation (put in small eval set):
- chat-short: "What's the weather like in Paris this week?" (low risk)
- code-small: "Write a Python function to parse JSON lines and extract keys" (higher risk)
- summarization: 800-token article -> 3-sentence TL;DR (medium risk)

Conversation-style TODOs for meeting:
- Ask SRE: what's current 99th distribution by client type? (Noah to fetch)
- Ask Product: customer tiers that would opt into aggressive cost-saving.

End of scratchpad. More later as sim results come in.

-- sylvia
